AI tools in pediatric primary care primarily support early identification of OW/OB risk, but evidence on workflow integration, sustained engagement, and long-term clinical impact remains limited. Future research should prioritize prospective, workflow-embedded studies, meaningful clinical outcomes, equity, privacy, governance, clinician training, and policy oversight.

title: AI in Neuro-Oncology: An Overarching Review.
desc: [Neuro-oncology] Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being applied across neuro-oncology domains to analyze complex, high-dimensional, multimodal data. Despite major advances in the biological understanding and classification of CNS tumors, clinical outcomes for many of them remain poor, reflecting intra- and inter-tumor heterogeneity and limitations of conventional reductionist approaches. AI offers a paradigm shift to capture this heterogeneity and provide quantitative, reproducible diagnostic, predictive, and prognostic insights. This article describes a joint effort across the Response Assessment in Neuro-Oncology (RANO) working groups to provide an overarching review of the AI use across six key domains of neuro-oncology: neuroimaging, neuropathology, laboratory medicine, neurosurgery, drug discovery, and clinical trials. Applications closest to clinical use include imaging segmentation and quantification, AI-assisted image reconstruction, DNA methylation-based classification, and workflow optimization. Radiogenomics, WSI-based molecular prediction, AI-guided surgical targeting, liquid biopsy interpretation, AI-guided drug discovery, digital twins, and in silico trials remain promising but require stronger prospective validation. Key challenges include limited availability of large diverse datasets, variability in data acquisition and reference standards, and limited external validation. This review provides a unifying framework for understanding the role of AI across neuro-oncology and highlights key considerations for its responsible implementation, emphasizing standardization, reproducibility, multi-institutional validation, and human oversight.

To systematically evaluate the existing literature on the use and performance of AI models in MDT decision-making for ENT cancer. Systematic review. Further research is required to optimize AI reliability and validate its clinical utility. desc: [Infectious diseases & clinical microbiology] Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly influencing healthcare, with growing relevance in infectious diseases and clinical microbiology. Although AI has shown promising performance in image analysis, molecular diagnostics, risk prediction, and clinical decision support, its routine implementation remains constrained by limited external validation, heterogeneous datasets, algorithmic bias, and challenges in generalizability and explainability. The review also discusses AI's emerging role in scientific writing and the ethical and practical considerations associated with its clinical adoption. Overall, current evidence suggests that AI should be regarded as a complementary decision-support technology whose safe and effective integration depends on rigorous validation, high-quality data, and appropriate clinical oversight.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Triage in Primary Care: A Scoping Review of Clinical Applicability.
source: PubMed · International journal of medical informatics
desc: [International journal of medical informatics] To map artificial intelligence (AI) systems developed for triage in primary care and describe their characteristics, performance and clinical applicability. A scoping review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA-ScR. PubMed, MEDLINE (via Ovid), Embase, Web of Science, CINAHL (via EBSCOhost), IEEE Xplore and the ACM Digital Library were searched until March 14th 2026. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data on system characteristics, triage function, performance, validation, safety, equity and implementation. Each system was charted by triage function and by whether it was patient-facing, clinician-facing or fully automated. Seventeen studies were included, published between 2013 and 2026 across 12 countries (14/17 high-income). Most were clinician-facing decision support (14/17), three had a patient-facing component and none were autonomous. Diagnostic or screening triage was the most common function (n = 7), followed by prioritisation (n = 4) and referral routing (n = 4). Only two performed urgency classification or self-triage. As a clinician aid, AI improved performance (fundus accuracy 82.8 % to 91.1 %; dermoscopy management sensitivity 72.9 % to 94.2 %), but standalone models sometimes fell below clinicians. Reported accuracy ranged from 41.2 % to 98.28 % and AUROC from 0.65 to 0.90, on heterogeneous outcomes. Validation was mostly internal (11/17), external in four. None reported a prospective randomised comparison or measured patient outcomes. AI triage in primary care is concentrated on clinician-facing diagnostic and referral tasks and is most valuable for augmenting clinician workflows, particularly non-specialists. The evidence base remains immature, constrained by internal validation, unreliable reference standards, sparse equity assessment and absent prospective outcome data. Future work should prioritise prospective, outcome-anchored evaluation, with attention to safety and equity.

title: Artificial intelligence-based prediction of cerebrospinal fluid leak in skull base surgery: a scoping review.

desc: [European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery] Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leak remains one of the most significant complications of skull base surgery, particularly in endoscopic endonasal and transsphenoidal approaches. Accurate risk stratification may improve surgical planning and reconstruction strategies. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based models have been increasingly investigated for CSF leak prediction; however, the evidence remains methodologically heterogeneous. This scoping review aimed to map the current literature and summarize data sources, modeling approaches, validation strategies, and reported performance. This scoping review followed PRISMA-ScR guidance. Eligibility was structured using the Population-Concept-Context framework. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for English-language studies published from 2019 to 2025. Two authors independently screened titles/abstracts and full texts and independently charted data using a standardized table; disagreements were resolved by consensus. Eligible original human studies applied AI/ML to predict perioperative surgical CSF leak or to derive an imaging biomarker for identifying spontaneous lateral skull-base CSF leak/encephalocele relevant to surgical assessment. No formal protocol was prepared or registered. Fifty-five records were identified, and nine primary studies met the eligibility criteria after duplicate removal and full-text assessment. Six studies predicted intraoperative CSF leak, two predicted postoperative leak, and one evaluated a deep-learning-derived CT biomarker for identifying spontaneous lateral skull-base CSF leak or encephalocele relevant to surgical assessment. Three studies used classical machine-learning methods, four used predominantly deep neural-network or convolutional-neural-network approaches, one compared classical models with a feedforward neural network, and one used a BERT-based natural-language-processing model. One study reported prospective temporal validation; none reported independent external validation at another institution. Among studies reporting AUC, values ranged from 0.69 to 1.00; accuracy, where reported, ranged from 70% to 98.33%. AI-based prediction of CSF leak is a promising but evolving field. Methodological heterogeneity and the absence of independent external validation constrain clinical translation. Future studies should prioritize standardized outcomes, multicenter datasets, and prospective validation to support integration into clinical decision-making.

title: Artificial intelligence-based tongue image analysis for non-invasive screening of gastric cancer, precancerous lesions, and related gastrointestinal disorders: a systematic review.
desc: [Frontiers in medicine] Gastric cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality, largely because many cases are diagnosed at an advanced stage. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy with histopathological confirmation is the diagnostic gold standard, but its invasiveness, cost, and limited accessibility restrict population-level use. title: Strategy for early diagnosis of pancreatic cancer.
desc: [Frontiers in gastroenterology (Lausanne, Switzerland)] Exocrine pancreatic cancer, particularly Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma, is regarded as one of the most aggressive cancers with a poor prognosis. Its bleak outlook mainly results from its silent progression, late diagnosis, and unreliable early detection methods. Globally, PC ranks among the leading causes of cancer-related deaths, and its incidence continues to increase. Because the pancreas is situated deep within the abdomen, early symptoms such as mild abdominal pain, fatigue, or weight loss are often vague. Most patients are only diagnosed after the disease has spread beyond the point where curative treatment is possible. Although surgery provides the best chance for long-term survival, only a small number of patients qualify for it at the time of initial diagnosis. Several factors increase the risk of developing PC, including chronic pancreatitis, smoking, obesity, inherited genetic mutations (like BRCA1/2), and new-onset diabetes (NOD), which has recently gained attention as a possible early warning sign. However, widespread screening for PC isn't yet practical because the disease is relatively uncommon and there are no highly accurate, non-invasive biomarkers. The most widely used blood test, CA 19-9, often gives unreliable results, while newer molecular approaches-like circulating tumor DNA, exosomal markers, microRNAs, and metabolomic profiles-are still being refined. Recent advances in imaging technology, artificial intelligence, and targeted screening for high-risk individuals hold promise for catching pancreatic cancer earlier. As we advance, combining multi-omics biomarkers with precision imaging may finally make earlier diagnosis-and improved survival-a reality for this devastating disease.

title: A multi-agent large language model (LLM) platform for structured medical anamnesis in outpatient care.
desc: [Frontiers in digital health] Medical anamnesis is fundamental to clinical decision-making, yet outpatient consultations often provide limited time for systematic information collection. This study investigates whether structured anamnesis acquisition can be redistributed to a pre-consultation phase using a framework-driven large language model (LLM) platform. We developed Symptio, a proof-of-concept multi-agent LLM platform that operationalises the SOCRATES, Review of Systems, and SAMPLE frameworks as machine-interpretable constraints within a human-in-the-loop workflow. The system was evaluated in 100 simulated outpatient scenarios. Generated anamneses were compared with reference-standard representations using structural agreement and field-level performance metrics. Full structural agreement across all three frameworks was achieved in 87% of scenarios. Framework-specific agreement reached 96% for SOCRATES, 88% for Review of Systems, and 93% for SAMPLE. Micro-averaged precision, recall, and F1-score were 99.04%, 98.54%, and 98.79%, respectively. Although no high-severity errors were identified, 58 field-level discrepancies, including 28 medium-severity errors, were observed, supporting the need for physician review of all outputs. The findings demonstrate the technical feasibility of acquiring structured anamnesis in a framework-driven manner within a process-oriented multi-agent LLM architecture under controlled conditions. The proposed approach enables the relocation of routine information collection to a pre-consultation phase while preserving physician authority through human-in-the-loop validation. Further studies are required to evaluate clinical safety, workflow impact, and effectiveness in real-world settings.

desc: [Unfallchirurgie (Heidelberg, Germany)] The challenging transformation of medicine in the twenty-first century, involving robotics, artificial intelligence (AI) and the digitalization of daily work routines, is hampered by bureaucratic hurdles, a shortage of skilled workers and socioeconomic pressures within an aging healthcare system. title: Artificial intelligence-enabled drug discovery: A growing but largely early-stage clinical pipeline.
desc: [Cancer treatment reviews] Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into pharmaceutical discovery, yet the extent to which AI-enabled assets have translated into clinical-stage programs remains incompletely characterized. We performed a cross-sectional descriptive analysis of therapeutic assets discovered or developed using AI approaches that had entered at least one interventional human clinical trial through March 1, 2026. We identified 129 AI-enabled therapeutic assets across 69 companies. Oncology was the dominant therapeutic area (74 assets, 57.3%), and small molecules accounted for the majority of the pipeline (103 assets, 79.8%). Among these assets, 72 (55.8%) had completed Phase 1 and 24 (18.9%) had completed Phase 2; only five had entered or completed Phase 3. The observed probability of success was 77.8% for Phase 1 and 19.5% for Phase 2. Forty-eight assets (37.2%) were classified as targeting a novel biological target. Among companies with available data, the median time from founding to Phase 1 entry was 6.5 years (IQR 4.0-9.2), median total funding raised was $186.7 million (IQR $48.1-$595.0 million), and the median employee count at clinical entry was 73 (IQR 32-129), with a median operational intensity of $2.72 million per employee. AI-enabled therapeutics are entering clinical testing at increasing scale, but most programs remain early in development, with few having advanced beyond Phase 2. This dataset provides a baseline for future evaluation of whether AI-enabled discovery ultimately improves regulatory approval rates and clinical outcomes.

title: Artificial intelligence algorithms for the prediction of cognitive decline and dementia: A theoretical-historical narrative review.
source: PubMed · Journal of Alzheimer's disease reports
desc: [Journal of Alzheimer's disease reports] Population aging has increased the prevalence of neurodegenerative disorders associated with dementia, with Alzheimer's disease remaining the leading cause worldwide. Early identification of individuals at risk of cognitive decline, particularly those with mild cognitive impairment, remains a major clinical and scientific challenge. In this context, artificial intelligence has emerged as a promising framework for prognostic modeling and for the identification of clinically relevant predictors of disease onset and progression. This narrative review provides a theoretical and historical synthesis of the main machine learning and deep learning approaches used to predict cognitive decline and dementia from multimodal data, including biomarkers, clinical and demographic variables, cognitive measures, and neuroimaging markers. The review examines the methodological evolution of the field, from traditional statistical approaches to ensemble methods and deep neural architectures, and discusses the growing role of multimodal and longitudinal data integration. It also highlights major unresolved issues, including limited external validation, reduced interpretability, restricted generalizability, and the gap between predictive performance and clinical implementation. Overall, artificial intelligence has substantially advanced prediction research in cognitive decline and dementia, but its routine clinical adoption will depend on more rigorous validation, improved transparency, and stronger integration between neuroscience, clinical practice, and data science.

Physical activity is measured with a research-grade accelerometer worn on the wrist for one week at the start, at six months and at eighteen months. title: Artificial intelligence and machine learning, a game changer in pharmaceutical development ? - An updated perspective arising from Journees Galeniques 2024.

desc: [European journal of pharmaceutical sciences : official journal of the European Federation for Pharmaceutical Sciences] Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are increasingly being applied across pharmaceutical development, from drug-property prediction and safety assessment to formulation design, model-informed development and clinical research. This perspective synthesizes discussions from Journées Galéniques 2024 and updates them in light of scientific and regulatory developments through 2026. ML enables prediction, pattern recognition, and data-driven decision-making, helping researchers identify drug targets, design new molecules, predict toxicity, and optimize drug properties. In formulation development, ML can improve solubility prediction, excipient selection, and formulation strategy by reducing trial-and-error approaches. AI-based models and imaging technologies can also enhance understanding of drug delivery systems and improve prediction of in vivo performance. However, much of the published literature remains retrospective and is based on small or heterogeneous datasets, with limited external, prospective or clinically relevant validation. Recent regulatory frameworks place increasing emphasis on a clearly defined context of use, risk-based assessment of model credibility, data governance, generalizability, human oversight and lifecycle management. AI and ML should therefore be viewed not as replacements for pharmaceutical science, but as increasingly powerful tools that can strengthen and accelerate it. Their broader impact will depend on high-quality, interoperable data, rigorous validation, integration with pharmaceutical and clinical expertise, and clear evidence of meaningful clinical, manufacturing or regulatory value.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Multimodal Neuroimaging Research on Depression: A Bibliometric Analysis.
desc: [Psychiatry investigation] To conduct a systematic bibliometric review of artificial intelligence (AI)-based multimodal neuroimaging research in depression, mapping its evolution, collaborative networks, and intellectual foundations to guide future translation. Records were retrieved from Web of Science Core Collection (search date: 1 September 2025) using terms for depression, neuroimaging modalities, and AI/machine learning (ML)/deep learning. English, peer-reviewed articles/reviews (2001-2025) were screened; 1,232 studies were retained after deduplication and filtering. Analyses included annual output trends, co-authorship networks (countries/institutions/authors), keyword co-occurrence clustering with burst detection, and co-citation/bibliographic coupling using VOSviewer (v1.6.20) and Bibliometrix (v4.5.1). Annual publications rose from <20/year to 202 in 2024; 2025 counts (n=173) reflect January-August only. The international network spans 42 countries/regions linked by 320 co-authorship ties (total link strength=1,228; density of approximately 0.37). USA, China, and the UK constitute the epistemic core, with expanding participation from India, Brazil, and Iran. Institutional and author overlays indicate a small-world, hierarchical organization (205 institutions; 10 collaboration communities; author network 168 researchers) characterized by a productive core and long tail. Six keyword clusters delineate a functional workflow: 1) biomarkers/phenotypes, 2) functional connectivity, 3) machine-learning/computational approaches, 4) multimodal/precision psychiatry, 5) diagnostic classification/algorithm development, and 6) structural imaging/comorbidity. Co-citation and coupling reveal a progression from early ML and connectivity foundations to deep/graph models, multimodal fusion, explainability, and treatment-oriented prediction. AI-based multimodal neuroimaging in depression has evolved into a coherent, translationally focused field. Current trends emphasize model validation, interpretability, and cross-site generalization, supported by expanding international collaboration. Future priorities include harmonized data sharing, explainable modeling, and theory-informed clinical translation.

title: Beyond binary dentistry: Should artificial intelligence think more like clinicians?
source: PubMed · European journal of oral sciences
desc: [European journal of oral sciences] Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly influencing dental diagnosis and clinical decision-making, yet many AI systems continue to represent disease and treatment outcomes through discrete categories. Although binary classification has contributed substantially to diagnostic performance, it does not always reflect how clinicians reason in practice. Dental decisions are frequently made under incomplete information, biological variability, and competing clinical findings, requiring dentists to weigh probabilities, alternative explanations, and degrees of confidence rather than simply choosing between two outcomes. This short communication argues that future dental AI should better represent this inherent clinical uncertainty. Fuzzy logic provides one possible conceptual framework, allowing partial membership and graded states rather than forcing complex biological conditions into rigid categories. Its potential value in dentistry extends beyond computation: it may help AI communicate uncertainty in ways that are more consistent with clinical reasoning. Such systems could provide graded diagnostic confidence, competing possibilities, or degrees of treatment suitability, rather than presenting apparently definitive answers. This approach may also support explainability and reduce inappropriate reliance on algorithmic recommendations. The future of dental AI may therefore depend not only on improving predictive accuracy, but also on representing the grey zones in which much of clinical dentistry takes place.

In real-time navigation, AI-augmented fluoroscopy and tomosynthesis platforms represent the clearest example of clinically deployed AI that improves lesion localisation and diagnostic yield for peripheral pulmonary nodules, while camera-based localisation and shared-control robotic systems remain largely preclinical. desc: [American journal of pharmaceutical education] To synthesize pharmacy-education evidence across artificial intelligence (AI) and digital simulation technologies, compare modalities by educational function, evidence maturity, implementation requirements, and risk, and derive a competency-first framework for curricular selection, implementation, assessment, and governance. A narrative search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science prioritized pharmacy-education studies and reviews published from 2018 through August 2026. Educational function, rather than AI status alone, provided the primary organizing principle. Simulation modalities mainly support standardized rehearsal, contextualized practice, feedback, visualization, and debriefing; adaptive systems and large language models (LLMs) can add personalization or generative dialogue; and AI-assisted assessment can support item development, feedback, and workflow. desc: [British journal of neurosurgery] Multimodal neuromonitoring has emerged as a cornerstone of modern neurocritical care for traumatic brain injury (TBI). Over the past decade, significant advances in monitoring technology, including brain tissue oxygenation, cerebral microdialysis, continuous electroencephalography, near‑infrared spectroscopy, cerebrovascular autoregulation assessment and non‑invasive techniques have enabled clinicians to individualize treatment strategies based on real‑time physiological data. Concurrently, artificial intelligence and machine learning are transforming data integration and prognostic modelling, and non‑invasive and wearable approaches are beginning to extend brain monitoring beyond high‑resource neuro‑ICUs. title: How much do language and context affect the accuracy of AI health advice?
desc: [BMJ health & care informatics] Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for health advice, but evidence on how performance varies across languages, topics and sources remains limited. We assess linguistic and contextual variation in Artificial Intelligence (AI) health-claim verification. We evaluated seven widely accessible LLMs using UK and European Union (EU) health-claim registers and 9088 journalist-vetted PUBHEALTH claims. The register-language analysis used authorised entries translated into 21 languages; status-labelled UK/EU extensions added non-authorised entries for diagnostic checks. PUBHEALTH claims spanned COVID-19, abortion, politics and general health across government, media and other source domains, including nature.com. Models classified claims as supported or unsupported using modal responses across repeated runs. Authorised-claim sensitivity was highest in English and closely related European languages and declined with syntactic distance from English. In status-labelled UK and EU register extensions, models recognised authorised claims but often overclassified non-authorised claims as supported. PUBHEALTH accuracy was lower and varied by topic and source; inaccuracy was highest for general-health claims and claims linked to nature.com. High authorised-claim sensitivity for English register claims can hide lower sensitivity in other languages and weaker performance in other public-health contexts. Training-data exposure, editorial framing and topic-specific tuning are plausible contributors to these gaps. LLM performance in health-claim verification varies substantially by language, topic and source. English-language performance does not reliably generalise across contexts, underscoring the need for multilingual, domain-specific evaluation before public-health deployment.

title: A deep learning-based silhouette gait detection framework for fall risk classification in Parkinson's disease.
desc: [Frontiers in neurology] Parkinson's disease (PD) is a rapidly growing neurodegenerative disorder associated with gait impairment, functional decline, and increased fall risk. Conventional clinical assessments rely heavily on brief observational scales and are limited by subjectivity and environmental bias. There is a pressing need for objective, quantitative, and scalable digital assessment tools to support precision management of PD. This study aimed to develop and validate a smartphone-video-based gait assessment system aligned with a clinically meaningful pathway encompassing PD screening, functional evaluation, and fall risk classification. In this cross-sectional observational study, patients with mild-to-moderate PD and age-matched healthy controls were recruited following Institutional Review Board approval. Gait videos were recorded using smartphone cameras and processed through a silhouette extraction pipeline. Spatiotemporal gait features were subsequently extracted using a MoviNet-based deep learning framework. A multi-task framework was developed to perform PD screening, activities of daily living functional grading based on the Schwab and England Activities of Daily Living (S&E ADL) scale, and fall risk classification. Model performance and generalizability were evaluated using subject-independent data partitioning and independent cross-site validation. A total of 40 participants were recruited. For PD screening, the model achieved an accuracy of 95.7%, a sensitivity of 96.6%, a specificity of 92.2%, and an AUC of 0.994 on the independent test set. For S&E ADL functional grading, the model achieved an overall accuracy of 88.5% across three functional categories (80, 90, and 100%). For fall risk classification, the model achieved an accuracy of 91.1%, a sensitivity of 68.4%, a specificity of 98.3%, and an AUC of 0.909. Overall, the framework demonstrated robust performance across PD screening, functional stratification, and fall risk classification tasks. This study developed a smartphone-video-based gait assessment framework using computer vision and deep learning. The proposed framework demonstrated strong performance in PD identification, severity estimation, and fall risk classification. Future work will expand validation across diverse populations and disease stages, while advancing toward multimodal integration and long-term home monitoring.

title: Beyond SELEX: AI-driven aptamers from sequence to structure to function.
desc: [Biotechnology advances] Conventional aptamer discovery by systematic evolution of ligands by exponential enrichment (SELEX) is often constrained by limited library capacity, PCR bias, and multi-round screening. The recent convergence of artificial intelligence with aptamer development is driving a paradigm shift from empirical screening toward rational, data-driven design. This Review presents a timely and comprehensive overview of AI integration across the entire aptamer development pipeline, with a particular emphasis on advances reported in 2024-2026. We begin by discussing bioinformatics databases and computational tools for high-throughput SELEX data analysis. We then review state-of-the-art strategies for secondary and tertiary structure prediction, including recent breakthroughs such as AlphaFold 3, RoseTTAFoldNA, and diffusion-based approaches. We also cover machine learning methods for aptamer-target interaction prediction, molecular docking, dynamics simulations, and free energy calculations. A major focus is placed on very recent AI-driven generative design, including diffusion models (AptaDiff), language model-based frameworks (InstructNA, GRAPE-LM), and reinforcement learning approaches (AiDTA) for de novo aptamer generation and optimization. Emerging applications of AI-designed aptamers in precision diagnostics, targeted therapy, and biosensing are also surveyed. Finally, we discuss current challenges and outline future directions toward closed-loop, interpretable AI frameworks for translational aptamer development. By synthesizing the latest computational and experimental advances, this Review aims to serve as a timely resource for researchers seeking to leverage AI for next-generation aptamer discovery.

title: Deep learning-based metal artifact reduction in CT for head and neck radiotherapy.
source: PubMed · Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
desc: [Physics and imaging in radiation oncology] Metal artifacts from dental fillings and implants compromise CT image quality, target delineation, and dose calculation accuracy in head and neck (H&N) radiotherapy. Previous reviews have largely focused on traditional metal artifact reduction methods and image quality metrics rather than radiotherapy-specific endpoints. This systematic review evaluates deep learning-based metal artifact reduction (DL-MAR) approaches for H&N radiotherapy, emphasizing technical advances and clinical dosimetric validation. Following PRISMA guidelines, PubMed, IEEE Xplore, and Scopus were systematically searched (updated April 2026) for studies assessing DL-MAR methods in H&N CT imaging and radiotherapy. Of 227 identified records, 40 studies (11 traditional MAR and 29 DL-MAR studies) met the inclusion criteria. Reported DL architectures included convolutional neural networks, generative adversarial networks, dual-domain networks, diffusion models, and task-oriented loss functions. Among studies with clinical dosimetric validation, GAN-based and task-oriented approaches consistently reported dose deviations below 3%. Gamma pass rates exceeding 95% (3%/3 mm) were reported in a subset of these studies. Dual-domain and diffusion-based methods were evaluated primarily using image quality metrics without direct radiotherapy-specific dosimetric validation. Current evidence suggests that DL-MAR may achieve clinically acceptable dosimetric accuracy while improving artifact suppression and target visualization in H&N radiotherapy planning. Task-oriented loss functions currently demonstrate promising potential for clinical translation based on available retrospective evidence. Broader clinical implementation remains limited by reliance on synthetic training data, restricted access to sinogram data, and the absence of prospective multicenter validation studies.

desc: [Journal of biomedical optics] Deep learning (DL)-based image reconstruction methods for photoacoustic computed tomography (PACT) have developed rapidly in recent years. A benchmarking framework is proposed that provides open-source, anatomically plausible synthetic datasets and evaluation strategies for DL-based acoustic inversion methods in PACT. The datasets each include over 10,000 two-dimensional (2D) stochastic breast objects with clinically relevant lesions and paired measurements at varying modeling complexity. The evaluation strategies incorporate both traditional and task-based IQ measures to assess fidelity and clinical utility. A preliminary benchmarking study is conducted to demonstrate the framework's utility by comparing DL-based and physics-based reconstruction methods. The benchmarking study demonstrated that the proposed framework enabled comprehensive, quantitative comparisons of reconstruction performance and revealed important limitations in certain DL-based methods. Although they performed well according to traditional IQ measures, they often failed to accurately recover lesions. This highlights the inadequacy of traditional metrics and motivates the need for task-based assessments. The proposed benchmarking framework enables systematic comparisons of DL-based acoustic inversion methods for 2D PACT. By integrating clinically relevant synthetic datasets with rigorous evaluation protocols, it enables reproducible, objective assessments and facilitates method development and system optimization in PACT.

title: Large language model-guided high-throughput screening for accelerated discovery of Pt-based high-entropy electrocatalysts.
desc: [Science bulletin] Pt-based high-entropy alloy (Pt-HEA) catalysts show significant potential for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), yet their vast compositional space challenges conventional trial-and-error approaches. Here, we propose a large language model (LLM)-guided closed-loop framework for high-throughput discovery to accelerate the rational design and optimization of Pt-HEA catalysts. The framework first extracts structured knowledge from extensive literature and incorporates retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to develop an LLM assistant tailored to HEA electrocatalysis research. The assistant transforms scattered literature knowledge, experimental constraints, and platform capabilities into experimentally feasible Pt-HEA candidate combinations and executable experimental protocols. High-throughput synthesis and screening enabled rapid evaluation of multiple Pt-HEA candidates, followed by Bayesian optimization to efficiently refine compositions within the representative Fe-Co-Ni-Cu-Pt system. This established a collaborative closed-loop workflow linking LLM-assisted candidate generation, high-throughput feedback, Bayesian optimization recommendations, density functional theory (DFT) mechanistic interpretation, and proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) device validation. Using this framework, we completed three iterative cycles involving 50 samples within 48 h, revealing how HER activity depends on atomic ratios in the Fe-Co-Ni-Cu-Pt system and identifying Fe30Co30Ni10Cu10Pt20 as the optimal composition. Theoretical calculations demonstrated that the multimetallic local coordination environment formed by Fe, Co, Ni, and Cu regulates the electronic structure of Pt active sites and fine-tunes the Pt-H interaction. Further PEMWE testing confirmed the catalyst's promising performance under device operating conditions. This work establishes a generalizable closed-loop paradigm integrating literature knowledge, experimental feedback, and model-driven decision-making, offering a viable route to the rational design and efficient optimization of complex multicomponent electrocatalytic materials.

title: [Dignity, ageing and artificial intelligence].
desc: [Soins. Gerontologie] Dignity is a concept frequently invoked in bioethics, both in the literature and in practice. However, those who use the term rarely describe or define it, despite the word's multiple meanings. This article explores its various meanings, highlighting the relational context in which it is situated, whether it is attributed or intrinsic. The discussion focuses on the impact of AI-powered assistive robots, designed to combat isolation and loneliness, as well as on relationality and dignity in the broadest sense.

title: Artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled RNA therapeutic design: from molecular optimization to system-level evaluation.
desc: [British journal of pharmacology] RNA therapeutics are increasingly moving from empirical screening towards rational, computation-guided design. Recent advances in RNA language models, generative models and structure-aware learning have improved sequence representation, candidate generation and structure-constrained optimization. However, favourable molecular properties do not necessarily translate into desirable biological performance, because therapeutic outcomes also depend on modality-specific mechanisms, delivery and exposure, molecular interactions, cellular state, immune responses and network-level adaptation. Here, we review AI-enabled RNA therapeutic design through the specific lens of the interface between molecular optimization and system-level evaluation. We compare the design constraints of siRNAs, antisense oligonucleotides, aptamers, mRNAs and translation-oriented circRNAs, and examine the capabilities and current limitations of sequence-, generative- and structure-based computational models. We further discuss the data resources and perturbation representations required to connect molecular candidates with broader cellular-response models. In this context, virtual cells are considered as approximate computational frameworks for candidate prioritization and risk-oriented system-level assessment rather than complete digital replicas of living cells. Finally, we outline a conceptual generation-simulation-feedback-optimization framework for integrating molecular design with progressively higher-level evaluation. This perspective emphasizes the need for better interfaces among RNA design, pharmacological context and cellular-response modelling, rather than relying on molecular optimization alone.

title: MechaScreener: Large language model-based automated screening for systematic reviews and research.
desc: [Research synthesis methods] Systematic reviews are the gold standard for evidence synthesis, but the manual title and abstract screening of thousands of references creates a severe bottleneck. Existing automated tools have historically struggled to achieve the near-perfect recall (sensitivity) required for reliable reviews. We developed MechaScreener as a 'zero-shot' automated screening tool that utilises a large language model to rank article relevance. The tool requires no initial training data or manual pre-screening, as MechaScreener directly applies user-provided question elements (PICO) or inclusion/exclusion criteria to assign an ordinal relevance score (1-5) to each reference. We evaluated the tool in two phases: a development phase using five reference libraries to optimise prompts, and an independent evaluation phase using 10 diverse Cochrane review libraries (comprising both randomised controlled trials [RCTs] and non-RCTs) containing over 58,000 references. In the evaluation dataset, MechaScreener achieved a perfect recall of 1.00 (100%) in all 10 reviews, ensuring that no relevant articles were missed (pooled record-level 95% CI: 0.98-1.00). Concurrently, it achieved an overall macro-average specificity of 0.61 (61%, cluster bootstrap 95% CI: 0.46-0.75; pooled record-level specificity 0.59, 95% CI: 0.59-0.60). Specificity varied from 0.21 in broad public health topics to 0.91 in precise pharmacological interventions, reflecting the tool's built-in conservatism when evaluating ambiguous abstracts. By safely eliminating over 60% of irrelevant literature during the initial screening phase without compromising recall, MechaScreener functions as a highly reliable but low-effort 'first-pass' filter, allowing researchers to substantially reduce manual workloads and reallocate resources towards full-text review and data extraction.

title: Biomedical retrieval-augmented generation for relation classification.
source: PubMed · Frontiers in research metrics and analytics
desc: [Frontiers in research metrics and analytics] The rapid expansion of biomedical literature requires automated methods for accurate and efficient information extraction. This study addresses relation classification: given a pair of annotated biomedical entities in a research article title and abstract, assigning the relation that holds between them from a pre-defined set. We evaluate a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework in which semantically similar annotated examples are retrieved from a training pool and supplied to a large language model as in-context demonstrations. Four open-source LLMs are compared against a supervised DeBERTa+CNN baseline on GutBrainIE, and four further corpora (ChemProt, BioRED, its BioCreative VIII release BC8, and DDI-2013) are used to test whether the findings generalize. We report macro- and micro-averaged precision, recall and F1-score, and the rate of predictions that fall outside the defined relation set. On GutBrainIE, Qwen3:14B with 25 retrieved examples reaches 0.877 macro and 0.866 micro F1, against 0.440 and 0.562 for the supervised baseline, while the smaller Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma3:12B models do not exceed the baseline on macro F1. Macro F1 rises from 0.105 without demonstrations to 0.877 with 25, with the steepest gains over the first ten retrieved examples and subsequent variation smaller than the run-to-run standard deviation. Predictions falling outside the defined relation set drop from 39 at zero shots to at most one between 20 and 35, so retrieval improves output validity as well as accuracy. Across the four further corpora these gains do not generalize uniformly: the best configuration exceeds the supervised baseline on ChemProt, improves macro but not micro F1 on BioRED and BC8, and falls below it on both measures on DDI-2013. Since DDI-2013 is the most balanced corpus in the set and, like ChemProt, is annotated within single sentences, that reversal is not explained by class imbalance or annotation scope, but is consistent with what the relation labels encode: whether they name relationships recoverable from biomedical knowledge, or boundaries set by an annotation guideline.

title: Automatic insect identification, counting, and monitoring techniques: a review.
desc: [Pest management science] Insect pests threaten agricultural productivity, while conventional surveillance is labour-intensive and excessive pesticide use creates environmental and health risks. This review evaluated automated insect detection, counting, classification and monitoring technologies, focusing on machine-learning integration, field transferability, and operational readiness. A PRISMA 2020-guided formal search covering publications from 2010 to 2024 identified 313 records relevant to the technological and methodological scope of the review. After title/abstract screening and full-text eligibility assessment, 116 publications were retained. The evidence encompassed camera- and vision-based systems; acoustic, infrared, and optoelectronic sensors; electrostatic and physical approaches; non-lethal photonic monitoring; radar and biosensing technologies; Internet of Things-enabled platforms; and machine- and deep-learning methods. Camera- and vision-based systems were among the most extensively documented and field-oriented approaches, particularly when integrated with remote image acquisition, communication networks, and automated classification. Acoustic systems provided complementary options for continuous or low-power monitoring, whereas radar, biosensing, and other emerging approaches broadened applications toward biodiversity assessment, large-area surveillance, and early detection. Reported performance was not directly comparable across publications because metrics, acquisition conditions, and validation levels differed substantially, ranging from laboratory or dataset benchmarks to semi-field trials, field validations, and operational deployments. No single technology is optimal for all monitoring objectives. Operational adoption requires standardized task-specific reporting, independent and sustained field validation, representative datasets, improved transferability across crops and environments, and system-level assessment of robustness, energy autonomy, connectivity, maintenance, and cost. Sensor fusion, edge artificial intelligence, and domain-adaptive or uncertainty-aware models are promising when they provide measurable decision-support benefits. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Toward brain-trained humanoid robots.
desc: [Frontiers in neurorobotics] A growing corpus of experimental research demonstrates that neuroimaging data can be leveraged to improve the performance of artificial intelligence models, including reinforcement learning models in robotics. However, most existing studies have focused on vision, audition, language, or reward and error signals recorded while the human brain acts as an observer. In this paper, we argue that humanoid robots, although not equivalent to humans, could offer a unique opportunity to use the neural signals associated with touch, or other embodiment-dependent neural signals. As a result, humanoid robots could significantly expand the range of brain regions and functional networks that could be targeted for brain-trained artificial intelligence, and open new horizons in terms of alignment and reasoning. We discuss the improvements that neuroimaging data could potentially unlock in the context of sensorimotor tasks, spatial navigation, sensorimotor integration, embodied alignment, embodied reasoning, and social integration, as well as the broader challenges and opportunities related to brain-trained humanoid robots.

title: Deep learning reveals ecological decoupling and rate heterogeneity in Hymenoptera wing evolution.
desc: [Science advances] Quantifying biomorphological evolution and integrating phenotypic data into large-scale ecological and evolutionary studies are often limited by the scalability, subjectivity, and poor interpretability of existing methods. We introduce HAIKA (Hierarchical Attention-based Interpretable K-dimensional Autoencoder), a self-supervised residual channel-attention autoencoder that extracts continuous morphological representations from unlabeled standardized images and highlights the image regions that contribute to those representations. Applied to insect forewings across broad pterygote lineages, HAIKA outperformed most baseline deep learning models and conventional descriptors in clustering, dimensionality reduction, and morphological embedding. When applied to Hymenoptera (i.e., ants, bees, and wasps), the HAIKA-derived continuous characters improved morphology-based phylogenetic reconstruction and illuminated the evolutionary dynamics of wing shape and venation. Our results reveal that wing morphological evolution in Hymenoptera proceeds at decoupled rates across shape and venation modules and is not consistently aligned with key ecological transitions such as parasitoidism or eusociality. HAIKA provides a scalable, image-based route for phenotypic analyses, broadly applicable across diverse taxa and to both 2D and 3D datasets.

title: Deep learning without weight symmetry.
desc: [PNAS nexus] Backpropagation (BP), a foundational algorithm for training artificial neural networks, predominates in contemporary deep learning. Although highly successful, it is widely considered biologically implausible, because it relies on precise symmetry between feedforward and feedback weights to accurately propagate gradient signals that assign credit. The so-called weight transport problem concerns how biological brains learn to align feedforward and feedback paths while avoiding the nonbiological transport of feedforward weights into feedback weights. To address this, several credit assignment algorithms, such as feedback alignment and the Kolen-Pollack rule, have been proposed. While they can achieve the desired weight alignment, these algorithms imply that if a neuron sends a feedforward synapse to another neuron, it should also receive an identical or at least partially correlated feedback synapse from the latter neuron, thereby forming a bidirectional symmetric connection. However, experimental studies of cortical connectivity do not support the widespread prevalence of such symmetric connections, and in fact report many unidirectional connections, thus imposing a biological constraint on credit assignment. We refer to the failure of existing algorithms to satisfy this constraint as the weight symmetry problem. To address this challenge of biological constraints on connectivity, we introduce the product feedback alignment (PFA) algorithm. We demonstrate that PFA can eliminate explicit weight symmetry entirely while closely approximating BP and achieving comparable performance in deep convolutional networks. Our results offer an approach to solve the longstanding problem of credit assignment in the brain, leading to more biologically plausible learning in deep networks compared to previous methods.

title: A new place for stories in conservation.
source: PubMed · Conservation biology : the journal of the Society for Conservation Biology
desc: [Conservation biology : the journal of the Society for Conservation Biology] Michael Soule writes in his foundational article "What is Conservation Biology?" that "in crisis disciplines, one must act before knowing all the facts; crisis disciplines are thus a mixture of science and art, and their pursuit requires intuition as well as information." Since this article was published three decades ago, conservation biology has largely focused its energies on formalizing and memorializing its scientific findings. There is no doubt this empirical turn has developed vital methods and tools, enabled links between science and policy, and fortified the discipline's credibility within the broader biological sciences. Nevertheless, Soule's intuition that conservation biology requires a kinship with art, and particularly with storytelling, remains essential to the discipline-particularly in an information environment saturated by generative artificial intelligence-in at least three important ways. First, as a crisis discipline, conservation biology remains firmly attached to questions of not only valuation but also value, which have always relied on stories and myth for expression and enrichment. Second, conservationists continue to find that stories are at least as effective as logic in communicating results and precipitating action. Fortunately, conservation science lends itself to narrative arcs by demonstrating evidence of change. Revelations of the degradation and restoration of biological diversity rhyme with myths of loss and redemption and create important roles for storytelling in conservation projects. Third, as the conservation tent continues to expand beyond understanding what humans have done to understanding why, there is an increasingly pressing need to listen to the stories that accompany human behavior. Conservation continues to thrive as an empirical discipline. Embracing the opportunities and obligations of storytelling will allow conservation to engage even more deeply with a complex world.

title: Current applications and challenges of artificial intelligence in orthopedic imaging: A narrative review.
source: PubMed · Journal of orthopaedic surgery (Hong Kong)
desc: [Journal of orthopaedic surgery (Hong Kong)] BackgroundArtificial intelligence (AI), especially machine and deep learning, is an emerging tool in medicine with growing applications in orthopedic imaging. Given imaging's central role in diagnosis, surgical planning, and treatment monitoring, this narrative review maps the current and potential uses of AI in orthopedics, identifies underdevelopment sections, and emphasizes limitations in clinical practice.MethodsA PubMed search used the terms "Orthopedic," "Imaging," and "Artificial Intelligence." Studies were screened by title and abstract, excluding non-orthopedic or non-AI studies, animal research, pediatric populations, and robotics or pharmacology papers. Eighty-five peer-reviewed articles were analyzed for imaging modality, clinical application, AI technique, and assigned a level of evidence. They were selected based on relevance to AI in orthopedic imaging.ResultsAI applications spanned radiography, CT, MRI, DTI, and ultrasound. For bone pathology, AI aided fracture detection and osteoarthritis prediction with clinician-level accuracy. In soft tissue injuries, models assisted in rotator cuff and meniscus tear detection and muscle segmentation. AI-driven 3D reconstructions and virtual reduction models enhanced surgical planning, particularly in joint replacement and trauma. Spine imaging benefited from vertebral segmentation, disc degeneration classification, and paraspinal muscle analysis, improving preoperative planning and outcome prediction. radiography, CT, MRI, DTI, and ultrasound. An important distinction is that many of these models generated outputs that surrounded conditional probabilities rather than categorical diagnoses. Many pitfalls remain including single-center overfitting, data leakage, and inter-reader variability.ConclusionsAI demonstrates potential to enhance diagnostic accuracy, streamline surgical planning, and improve workflow efficiency. Challenges remain, including data bias, regulatory constraints, and ethical considerations, warranting caution to its blanket application in medicine. Continued integration and validation are needed for optimal clinical use.Clinical RelevanceAI may serve as an adjunct to clinicians, supporting imaging interpretation and surgical decision-making while preserving human judgment.

Applications of artificial intelligence in personalized nutrition interventions.
desc: [Frontiers in nutrition] Unhealthy dietary patterns remain a major modifiable contributor to the global burden of obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), cardiovascular disease, and cancer. However, individuals can respond markedly differently to identical foods, limiting the effectiveness of one-size-fits-all dietary guidance. This review examines the application of artificial intelligence (AI) to personalized nutrition interventions across three interconnected layers. At the biological level, inter-individual variability can be characterized by three mechanistic dimensions: nutrigenomic variation, which influences nutrient metabolism and disease susceptibility; metabolomic biomarkers, which objectively capture dietary exposure and early metabolic alterations; and the gut microbiome, which bidirectionally mediates diet-host interactions. At the technological level, AI integrates these dimensions into multimodal digital profiles. Machine learning models predict individual postprandial glycemic and lipemic responses, with reported correlations of up to r = 0.77 in large cohorts; deep learning and computer vision automate dietary assessment; natural language processing and large language models (LLMs) support nutrition counseling; knowledge graphs enable constraint-aware food recommendations; and digital-twin and adaptive closed-loop systems incorporating continuous glucose monitoring and wearable-device data support real-time nutritional interventions. However, the strength of clinical evidence varies across disease domains. Glycemic management in T2DM and prediabetes currently has the most mature randomized controlled trial evidence: an AI-enabled personalized intervention combining algorithmic dietary personalization with CGM-linked feedback improved glycemic endpoints compared with a Mediterranean diet, while a fully automated AI-delivered diabetes prevention program achieved outcomes non-inferior to those of human coaching. title: Wearable Technologies for Cancer Therapy and Monitoring: A Comprehensive Review.
source: PubMed · Critical reviews in biomedical engineering
desc: [Critical reviews in biomedical engineering] Wearable devices have emerged as pivotal innovations in oncology, revolutionizing cancer therapy and monitoring through continuous, non-invasive physiological tracking. This comprehensive review examines the integration of advanced wearable technologies-such as electrocardiography (ECG), photoplethysmography (PPG), infrared thermometers, galvanic skin response (GSR) meters, and pulse oximeters-in detecting biomarkers associated with cancer progression and treatment efficacy. By leveraging real-time data acquisition, these devices enable early identification of conditions like chemotherapy-induced cardiotoxicity, evidenced by ECG-derived AI models predicting cardiomyopathy risks with 2-5-fold accuracy, and PPG-based systems detecting vascular anomalies indicative of malignancies. The incorporation of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) algorithms further enhances diagnostic precision, exemplified by AI-ECG tools that dynamically forecast cardiotoxicity 12-24 months prior to clinical onset. Additionally, wearable drug delivery mechanisms, including microneedle patches for localized chemotherapy and programmable ambulatory pumps, are explored for their capacity to optimize therapeutic outcomes while mitigating adverse effects. A systematic analysis of literature sourced from Google Scholar, PubMed, and ScienceDirect underscores the transformative potential of these technologies in fostering personalized oncology care, as demonstrated by clinical trials such as the EMBRaCE program, which reported enhanced patient recovery through continuous monitoring. Despite these advancements, challenges related to motion artifact interference, data heterogeneity, and ethical concerns regarding AI transparency necessitate resolution for widespread clinical adoption. Future trajectories highlight the convergence of multimodal sensor networks with AI-driven analytics to establish autonomous monitoring systems, thereby redefining precision oncology. This review underscores the critical role of wearable devices in advancing theranostic paradigms, advocating for their integration into mainstream oncology to improve early detection, treatment personalization, and overall patient prognoses.

title: Artificial intelligence-enabled clinical phenotyping of human brown fat.
desc: [Nature] Adipose tissue has a central role in systemic energy balance and the pathogenesis of obesity and its sequelae1,2. In contrast to white adipose tissue, brown adipose tissue (BAT) uses energy to produce heat3. Detectable BAT in humans is associated with decreased prevalence of cardiometabolic diseases4. However, the complete spectrum of health conditions associated with BAT remains unknown, and high-throughput methods to quantify BAT activity in humans are lacking5,6. Here we leveraged big data and artificial intelligence to systematically define the clinical impact of BAT in a cohort of 101,243 patients from a large cancer centre. Our unbiased analyses revealed that, across all diagnoses, cardiovascular and psychiatric diseases were less prevalent in people with BAT. Using a machine learning approach, we semi-automatically quantified BAT activity in approximately 8,700 patients and demonstrated that higher BAT activity, especially in the axillary depot, is associated with lower odds of cardiometabolic diseases and healthier white fat distribution. People with BAT also exhibited more favourable glycaemic parameters, lipid profiles, inflammatory markers and echocardiographic indices. Analysis of medication usage demonstrated that angiotensin receptor blocker use was positively associated with BAT presence. As proof of concept, we showed that the angiotensin receptor blocker losartan increased brown adipocyte activity and whole-body energy expenditure. Altogether, our studies harnessing artificial intelligence and big data identify new clinical phenotypes linked to BAT and serve as a platform for drug repurposing to activate this tissue in humans.

title: Operationalizing clinical artificial intelligence through secure FHIR pipelines: a zero-trust cloud reference architecture for EHR interoperability.
desc: [Frontiers in digital health] Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) standardizes clinical exchange but does not establish that a downstream artificial intelligence (AI) use remains authorized, semantically consistent, or accountable. This Hypothesis and Theory article proposes evidence-continuous boundary control: a material data, model, or workflow transition is governed by an applicable policy decision and linked to versioned evidence of its prerequisites, execution, and disposition. The framework arose from continuing healthcare-interoperability research and was formalized through standards analysis, targeted evidence synthesis, and explicit design inference. Documented revision searches distinguish external evidence from architectural decisions. Eight requirements are organized into five functional layers: clinical sources, an interoperability edge, a zero-trust control plane, a segregated cloud data and AI plane, and governance and monitoring. Applications are consumers, not a sixth layer. An illustrative adult readmission-risk workflow connects identity, policy, source versions, features, model release, scoring, presentation, and human action. Its symbolic FHIR R4 evidence linkage includes explicit R5 translation cautions and policy-aware authorization, including consent where applicable. Six propositions test incremental value against a well-run contemporary platform without removing its native safeguards; simulated ablations isolate particular links. Independent reference standards, denominators, support, counterevidence, and inconclusive conditions expose operational and human-factors trade-offs. A bounded synthetic-data companion implementation makes selected exchange controls inspectable; it does not implement the complete clinical-AI architecture or validate its propositions. No empirical architecture evaluation, patient dataset, clinical effectiveness, or independent expert validation is reported. Staged future studies must establish incremental benefit without disproportionate burden or inappropriate reliance.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Predicting Amputation and Related Outcomes in Peripheral Artery Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
desc: [Annals of vascular surgery] Peripheral artery disease (PAD) affects over 236 million individuals globally and carries substantial risks of amputation, major adverse limb events (MALE), and mortality. Existing clinical scoring systems focus on short-term surgical outcomes and lack generalizability. Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a promising tool for PAD outcome prediction. To conduct the first quantitative meta-analysis evaluating the discriminative performance, methodological rigor, and certainty of evidence of ML-based prognostic models for adverse limb outcomes in PAD. Following PRISMA/PRISMA-S guidelines, PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception through March 15, 2026. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and PROBAST risk-of-bias assessment. Random-effects meta-analysis (DerSimonian-Laird with Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman correction) and hierarchical summary ROC (HSROC) analysis were performed; certainty was rated with GRADE. Ten studies were included. The pooled AUC for amputation-related outcomes was 0.88 (95% CI, 0.83-0.94; prediction interval, 0.79-0.98) with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 95.4%). HSROC yielded pooled sensitivity 0.855 and specificity 0.836. Registry-based studies showed higher pooled AUC than non-registry studies (0.92 vs 0.80; p = 0.004). All models had high or unclear risk of bias in the analysis domain; none underwent independent external validation. GRADE certainty was very low. ML models demonstrate high discriminative performance for predicting amputation-related outcomes in PAD, but very low certainty of evidence, absence of external validation, and high risk of bias currently limit clinical implementation. Prospective multicenter validation and adherence to AI reporting guidelines are essential before clinical translation.

title: Deep learning-based super-resolution reconstruction for improved image quality in shoulder MRI.
desc: [European journal of radiology] To compare the image quality of shoulder Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) using three imaging acquisition or reconstruction approaches-Parallel Imaging (PI), Compressed Sensing (CS), and Deep Learning-Based Super-Resolution Reconstruction (SR)-and to evaluate reader-assessed image quality and preference. A retrospective study included 60 patients (27 males, 33 females; mean age 53.67 ± 12.11 years). Shoulder MRI was performed with PI, CS and SR (reconstructed from CS data) across six sequences. Quantitative and qualitative assessments were conducted by experienced observers. Three radiologists selected clinically preferred sequences after a 2-week washout. Consistency and inter-group comparisons were statistically analyzed. The quantitative and qualitative assessment between observers showed good consistency. The SR group showed significantly higher quantitative measurements across all six sequences of structures [e.g. SNR: Supraspinatus tendon SR 14.03 (10.60, 20.26), CS 11.87 (8.39, 15.96), PI 8.75 (5.18, 13.51), P < 0.001] than PI and CS. SR images generally showed lower edge rise distance (ERD) values, significant overall differences among PI, CS, and SR (P < 0.01), Qualitative assessment revealed that SR overall differences among PI, CS and SR, with statistically significant differences (P < 0.001). Furthermore, three reader preference results indicated a preference for SR images that all readers preferred SR images (86 %, 92 %, and 93 %). Compared to PI and CS, SR significantly improves image quality in shoulder MRI without increasing acquisition time. SR enhances the visualization of fine anatomical structures, providing improved image quality and supporting its potential application in clinical shoulder MRI.

title: Human β defensin type 2 based novel antimicrobial peptide prediction using both molecular dynamics simulation and artificial intelligence methods.
desc: [Frontiers in chemistry] The global health crisis triggered by SARS-CoV-2 has highlighted the urgent need for effective treatments. Although several anti-viral drugs targeting SARS-CoV-2 have been developed, there remains considerable interest in exploring natural antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) secreted by the human innate immune system as alternative therapeutic agents. Human β defensin type 2 (hBD-2) has been found to bind to the receptor-binding domain (RBD) of SARS-CoV-2 and block the virus entry. In order to design effective anti-virial drugs based on hBD-2, 32 block-mutants (mutation at more than one site simultaneously) were designed, and their interaction with RBD were predicted in terms of structural stability and binding energy. In combination with data from a total of 247 hBD-2 point-mutants reported in our previous work, artificial intelligence (AI) models were trained to design more efficient hBD-2 variants. With that, advanced AI approaches, including convolutional neural network (CNN) and long short-term memory (LSTM) models were employed to predict hBD-2 mutant sequences with potentially enhanced binding affinity with RBD compared with the wildtype peptide. Based on the predicted sequences, the AlphaFold program was applied to predict the structures of AMPs, and then all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were performed to calculate the binding interaction energies between each hBD-2-based AMP and the RBD as a measure of binding affinity. Structural stability was also evaluated through analyses of Root Mean Square Deviation (RMSD), Root Mean Squared Fluctuation (RMSF), the number of hydrogen bonds formed, and buried surface area. The results indicate that several AMPs exhibited more stable binding with RBD than the wildtype, highlighting their potential as novel hBD-2-derived antiviral candidates against SARS-CoV-2. Furthermore, based on the obtained results, the LSTM model demonstrated greater effectiveness than the CNN model in designing novel hBD-2-based anti-virial drugs against CoV-2.
